Size ladder

The app draws this at roughly 100×56 pt. Everything to the left of the 2× mark is the size that actually ships, so that is the one to judge.

The pinch, frame by frame

Index and thumb rotate about their own knuckles, and the frame is redrawn from where the fingertips actually land — the same relationship FrameTracker uses, where the quad corners are [leftIndex, rightIndex, rightThumb, leftThumb]. Pinching therefore shrinks the frame, which is the thing the gesture really does.

Why not Lottie

  • The animation is one morphing outline. Every pose is the same 112-point loop, resampled so a given vertex is the same piece of anatomy in every frame, so the whole thing is a single <animate attributeName="d"> plus a mirrored <use>. That is native SMIL, supported in Safari, Chrome and Firefox, and needs no runtime.
  • iOS would pay for Lottie twice. lottie-ios is a package dependency plus a JSON asset, to play back keyframes SwiftUI can interpolate itself: the poses are just angles, so HandFrameGlyph can keep its Canvas and animate two Doubles.
  • It stays truthful. The generator that made this page is checked in at design/hand-frame/tools/. Change a joint angle, re-run, and the SVG, the stills and the port all move together — a baked Lottie file would drift from the geometry the tracker uses.
  • If Lottie is wanted anyway, the hard part is already done: hand-frame-poses.json holds the three poses as matching vertex lists, which is exactly the shape a Lottie path keyframe takes.

How it is wired in
  • The glyph box went from 100×56 to 200×104 (same 1.9:1 ballpark), so the call site is now .frame(width: 112, height: 58).
  • enum FF keeps handFill, handStroke and frameStroke, retuned to 0.05 / 0.42 / 0.5; handDigit is gone, since the digits are part of the silhouette now.
  • The port bakes the three pose outlines into HandFrameGlyph.swift and lerps the point arrays inside a TimelineView capped at 30fps — the display link is wasted on motion this slow, and this is the busiest screen in the app.
  • The illustration is decorative, so it is accessibilityHidden inside the block's existing accessibilityElement(children: .combine), and it honours accessibilityReduceMotion by holding the rest pose.
